newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia seen buying U.S. corn on price falls.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia seen buying U.S. corn on price falls.

text.p: Indonesian corn prices were stable on Tuesday on ample stocks, while traders said a fall in U.S. corn prices could prompt Indonesian imports.
"I think there will be some interest in U.S. corn, especially because the local harvest in East Java might be affected by the on-going drought," one trader said.
He said declines in U.S. corn prices due to good weather in the growing region of the U.S. Midwest could prompt some importers to place orders for delivery later in the year.
"If they were to wait for too long, and the harvest is affected by the drought, they might be in trouble," he added.
The East Java is expected to peak at the end of the year.
Chicago corn futures closed lower on Monday and contract lows were set in most months with excellent weather again hitting the market.
July was down 4-1/4 cents at $2.40-1/2 per bushel while December was four cents lower at $2.29-1/4.
Some parts of densely-populated Java island have been experiencing severe drought conditions, but experts have said the weather was seasonal and not related to the El Nino factor.
Scientists have said the El Nino weather pattern is forming in the Pacific which has the potential to cause drought and damage billions of dollars worth of crops.
Another trader said Indonesia was flush with corn, with imports continuing to arrive from the United States, China and South America.
"There's plenty of corn coming in from everywhere. I don't think we will be requiring that much at the moment," he added.
Traders said corn was quoted 380-385 rupiah/kg in Jakarta, compared with 380 rupiah a week ago. Soymeal was quoted unchanged at 885-890 rupiah.
